parsed_profile.title: 7 & 9 F-CLASS TURBINE 1-2 SPACER WHEEL RIM INSPECTION RECOMMENDATIONS
parsed_profile.purpose: Communicate inspection recommendations to help mitigate the risk of possible damage to the gas turbine associated with turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim cracking and possible rim section liberation.
parsed_profile.compliance_category_text: Alert - Failure to comply with the TIL could result in equipment damage or facility damage. Compliance is mandated within a specific operating time.
parsed_profile.recurring_indicator_if_found: Non-recurring; considered complete once the inspection is completed and dispositioned. Further inspections completed as part of rotor life extension processes.
parsed_profile.coarse_outage_type: Hot Gas Path or Major Inspection
scope_of_work: Upon removal of the turbine shell casing for the hot gas path or major outage, perform a thorough cleaning of the rim of the 1-2 turbine spacer wheel to remove any oil and/or residual debris from the outer surface (approximately one shift, ~8 hours).
Perform ultrasonic inspection of the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim region (approximately two shifts, ~12-16 hours).
service_recommendation_line_items: Perform ultrasonic inspection of the rim region of the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel at the first outage (either hot gas path or major inspection) once the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel has accumulated 80,000 factored fired hours of operation (approximate range for inspection is 80,000 to 96,000 factored fired hours).
Engage GE's Inspection & Life Extension Services (I&LES) group to accurately perform the recommended inspection of the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim regions.
Inspect both forward and aft rim arms of the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel.
If indications are observed during inspection, contact GE service representative for assistance with disposition of the findings.
parsed_profile.completion_criteria_text: This TIL is considered complete once the inspection mentioned in the recommendations section is completed and dispositioned. Further inspections will be completed as a part of any rotor life extension processes.
parsed_profile.maintenance_trigger_text: Turbine 1-2 spacer wheel has accumulated 80,000 factored fired hours of operation.
recommended_interval_or_trigger: First outage (hot gas path or major inspection) once 80,000 factored fired hours accumulated
Approximate range for inspection is 80,000 to 96,000 factored fired hours
parsed_profile.usage_counter_requirements_text: Inspection required once the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel has accumulated 80,000 factored fired hours of operation (approximate range for inspection is 80,000 to 96,000 factored fired hours).
parsed_profile.frame_or_model_applicability_text: Select frame 7 and 9 F-class gas turbine rotor 1-2 spacer wheels (F-class definition includes specific F, FA, and FB rotors)
parsed_profile.hardware_or_part_configuration_text: Turbine 1-2 spacer wheel produced utilizing a high nickel alloy of a similar nature to the stage 1 and 2 turbine wheels.
parsed_profile.serial_or_unit_applicability_text: Select frame 7 and 9 F-class gas turbine rotor 1-2 spacer wheels with higher operational temperatures and specific environmental conditions.
parsed_profile.prerequisite_outage_or_inspection_contex: Requires removal of the turbine shell casing for hot gas path or major outage access.

parts_referenced.context: Turbine 1-2 spacer wheel (high nickel alloy) - forward and aft rim arms requiring ultrasonic inspection
Specialized ultrasonic equipment available with the GE I&LES inspection team

reference_documents.context: Fleet experience associated with TIL-1937 regarding rotors operating in higher operational temperatures and humid or corrosive conditions posing increased risk of crack initiation and propagation in rim arms.

parsed_profile.configuration_summary: Applicable to select frame 7 and 9 F-class gas turbine rotor 1-2 spacer wheels (F, FA, FB rotors) operating in higher operational temperatures and specific environmental conditions (humid or corrosive). Units must have accumulated 80,000+ factored fired hours.
severity_signals: Rim section liberation during full load operation
Significant collateral damage to compressor and turbine sections
Inter-granular crack propagation consistent with hold time fatigue
failure_consequences: Turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim section liberation during full load operation
Ejection of material into the hot gas path resulting in significant collateral damage to the compressor and turbine sections
Metal piece lodging into cooling slot of turbine wheel 1
parsed_profile.risk_summary: Rotors operating in higher operational temperatures and humid or corrosive conditions may pose an increased risk of crack initiation and propagation in the 1-2 spacer wheel rim arms. Cracks initiate from the internal surface and propagate radially and circumferentially outward until the rim can no longer sustain centripetal forces, resulting in rim section liberation and significant collateral damage to the gas turbine.

source_snippets.snippet: Communicate inspection recommendations to help mitigate the risk of possible damage to the gas turbine associated with turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim cracking and possible rim section liberation.

GE recommends performing an ultrasonic inspection of the rim region of the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel at the first outage (either hot gas path or major inspection) once the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel has accumulated 80,000 factored fired hours of operation (approximate range for inspection is 80,000 to 96,000 factored fired hours).
This ejection of material into the hot gas path resulted in significant collateral damage to the compressor and turbine sections of the gas turbine.

Further inspections will be completed as a part of any rotor life extension processes, therefore this TIL is considered complete once the inspection mentioned in this recommendations section is completed and dispositioned.
rotors operating in higher operational temperatures and humid or corrosive conditions may pose an increased risk of crack initiation and propagation in the rim arms

a thorough cleaning of the rim of the 1-2 turbine spacer wheel is required to remove any oil and/or residual debris from the outer surface. This required cleaning can be completed in approximately one shift (~8 hours). Ultrasonic inspection of the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim region can be completed in approximately two shifts (~12-16 hours).
